jobs.title: Robotics Machine Learning Engineer
jobs.description:
**Pantograph** is building general purpose intelligent robots that can safely and autonomously accomplish useful work in the real world. We believe the path to capable robots runs through general intelligence rather than narrow, robot-specific skills, and that there is an enormous amount of work worth doing in the physical world that would improve quality of life for people. As AI models make it easier to build software around our needs, we hope robots can empower people to shape the physical world.

Across research, hardware, and software, we focus on finding simple ideas that work, executing them extremely well, and scaling them up. We value clear thinking, careful execution, and systems we can understand, trust, and improve.

We're looking for a robotics ML engineer to design and build the systems that turn capable AI models into robots doing useful work. You'll bring a deep background in robotics and use it to decide how frontier models, learned policies, and classical controllers fit together. We see frontier models as an increasingly powerful foundation for general robot behavior, and want someone who can combine their capabilities with the methods robotics already does well.

The work includes connecting models to robot observations and actions, building the tools, skills, and controllers they rely on, and developing evaluations in simulation and on our fleet. You'll investigate when a frontier model should act directly, when it should coordinate faster learned policies or classical controllers, and when it should write its own tools or control code. You'll weigh the tradeoffs in capability, reliability, latency, safety, and how easily we can understand and supervise the system, with real deployments guiding your decisions.

You'll work closely with our research, robot software, and product teams, building a tight loop between experiments and experience on real hardware. We're looking for someone who combines excellent experimental judgment with a strong intuition for both robots and models, and enjoys building things to test their ideas. When something fails, you'll work out whether it calls for a better observation, a different tool, a change in orchestration, a better policy or controller, or a fix elsewhere in the system.

You might be a good fit if you:

* Have deep experience in robotics across areas such as control, perception, planning, and learned policies, and have made robots do useful work on real hardware
* Use simulation to develop and test systems, and understand where it diverges from reality
* Have designed and shipped robotic or AI systems that people use, with clear evidence of what made them better
* Are excellent at designing experiments and interpreting results: separating competing explanations, identifying confounders, and knowing what the evidence does and doesn't establish
* Have a strong intuition for how models behave: what they understand, what confuses them, and how their behavior changes with the tools, context, and feedback they receive
* Enjoy digging into failures and understanding how systems behave beyond aggregate metrics
* Are pragmatic about methods and care more about what works on real tasks than what's newest or most complex
* Can build reliable software across the stack, from model APIs and inference to robot software and testing infrastructure
* Communicate clearly and enjoy working across research and engineering
* Use AI tools extremely effectively

Bonus if you've worked with:

* Agent harnesses, tool use, memory, or long-horizon tasks
* Systems where models write and execute code or develop their own tools
* Fine-tuning vision-language-action models or other large robot policies
* Teleoperation, robot data collection, or learning from fleet data
* Evaluation design, failure analysis, or safety testing
* Inference optimization, including latency, throughput, and cost

We care much more about what you've built and learned than credentials. We're a small, fast-moving team working together in person in San Francisco. If this sounds exciting to you, we want to hear from you.

Compensation Range: $150K - $260K

This role is focused on modern SLAM techniques—both classical and learning-based—with an emphasis on scalable state estimation, sensor fusion, and long-term mapping in complex, dynamic environments.

This is a hands-on, research-driven role for someone who enjoys working at the intersection of robotics, computer vision, and probabilistic inference. You’ll collaborate closely with research scientists, ML engineers, and systems teams to translate cutting-edge SLAM ideas into production-ready capabilities that form the backbone of our world modeling stack.

====================

* Design and implement modern SLAM systems for real-world environments, including visual, visual-inertial, lidar, or multi-sensor configurations.

* Build and maintain scalable state estimation frameworks, including factor graph optimization, filtering, and smoothing techniques.
* Develop sensor fusion strategies that integrate cameras, IMUs, depth sensors, lidar, or other modalities to improve robustness and accuracy.
* Analyze failure modes in real-world SLAM deployments (e.g., perceptual aliasing, dynamic scenes, drift) and design principled solutions.
* Create evaluation frameworks, benchmarks, and metrics to measure SLAM accuracy, robustness, and performance across large datasets.
* Optimize performance across the stack, including real-time constraints, memory usage, and compute efficiency, for large-scale and production systems.

* Contribute to technical direction by proposing new research ideas, mentoring teammates, and helping define best practices for localization and mapping across the organization.

* Proficiency in Python and/or C++, with hands-on experience building research or production-grade SLAM systems.

UC Berkeley and UCSF have launched a joint program called the Bakar Computational Biomedicine Initiative to develop the frontier of AI and biomedicine, tremendously accelerating advances in clinical care. As part of this effort, at BIDS our team of open source research software engineers (OS-RSEs), product managers, and computational postdoctoral researchers will build the BioJupyter platform. Beacon Holdings is acquiring and operating a portfolio of vertical SaaS companies. Most private equity firms scale by adding people. We are building Beacon to scale by adding software. The thesis is simple. Portfolio operations, value creation, and deal sourcing are bottlenecked by human attention, and the right software platform can lift that ceiling by an order of magnitude.

We are building that platform: an agentic operating system that our portfolio companies run on. It is a problem set with real data, real multi-tenant requirements, and very few precedents to copy from.

Beacon has raised $750M+ from investors including General Catalyst, Lightspeed, D1 Capital, CPMG, and the family offices of the founders of Stripe, DoorDash, and Ramp.

**About the Role**
------------------

Members of Technical Staff (MTS) build the platform that everything else at Beacon runs on. You will own a piece of it end-to-end: design, implementation, operations, and long-term technical direction. This is a Staff Engineer role in everything but name. We run flat.

We are hiring for two roles. The bar is the same; the specialty differs.

* **Product and platform engineering.** A senior engineer who builds agentic products and the platform underneath them: services, APIs, data access, and deploy infrastructure. Works directly with the people who use them.
* **AI infrastructure.** An engineer who builds the systems around models: serving, retrieval, evals, observability, fine-tuning, and deployment into secure and regulated environments.

Both seats ship to real businesses, fast. You take a problem from the first conversation with a user to a system in production, and measure success by whether people use it.

**What You'll Do**
------------------

* You will own one or both of these areas end-to-end:

  + **Agentic products.** Build the AI-native tools that operators across our portfolio use every day. You own the full stack: agent loops, UI, internal APIs, and the deploy infrastructure other engineers build on. The bar is not demos. It is tools people choose to open on Monday morning.
  + **AI infrastructure.** Serve and operate models, including open-weight ones, across cloud, VPC, and isolated environments. Fine-tune open-weight models on proprietary data where a general model falls short. Build the retrieval and governed data access that ground agents in real business data. Choose which model handles which job, with cost, latency, and quality as explicit trade-offs.
* **Evals and observability.** Build the harness that tells us whether the system is working: task-level evals from real workflows, traces and telemetry, replay, and regression suites that catch quality drops before users do. Use the same signals to speed up root-cause analysis when things break.
* How you will work:

* **Ship to real businesses, fast.** Take a problem from the first user conversation to a system in production.
* **Prove quality with data.** No model or prompt change ships on vibes.
* **Work agent-first.** Agents are part of how you build, not just what you build.

Your Team Responsibilities:

Private capital index calculation is a demanding engineering problem. Inputs are irregular, sparse and often revised. The measures are non-linear and solver-based, and the published output is a number that clients rely on for a decade. Every run must reproduce bit-for-bit against the validated code. You will build the calculation library itself, including the plugin contract, the solver, the aggregation logic and the test harness that confirms results have not changed.

Your Key Responsibilities:

* Design and build the measure library: money-weighted (IRR, pooled, neutrally weighted), multiples, time-weighted (Modified Dietz, unitised, index-level chaining), public-market equivalents (Direct Alpha, KS-PME, Long-Nickels) and real-asset measures, each exposed through a stable, versioned, conformance-tested interface.
* Implement numerically sound logic: exact decimal arithmetic throughout, no floating-point types for money or IRR solves, a safeguarded solver that brackets before iterating, and a canonical flow order for summation.
* Make every calculation reproducible: pin each run to a data snapshot, engine version, measure version and input hash, so replays produce identical output and any mismatch is flagged.
* Build and maintain the conformance harness: golden vectors from the methodology documents run on every build, with invariant tests for date-shift, netting, weight sums and monotonicity.
* Optimise batch performance across roughly 15,000 funds and roughly 150 definitions in a single pass rather than 150 separate passes, with caching keyed on the data snapshot so re-ingested extracts invalidate stale results.
* Work with methodology, data and product teams to turn methodology documents into tested code, and review changes to numerical code.

Your skills and experience that will help you excel:

* Strong software engineering experience in a typed language, with linting and tests that enforce numerical rules and act as the specification.
* Working knowledge of fixed-precision and floating-point arithmetic, and a clear sense of where the two must never mix.
* Root-finding and numerical methods, including bracketing, convergence, ill-conditioning, and recognising when a converged result is still meaningless.
* A disciplined testing habit: test claims rather than asserting them, since plausible but wrong numbers are the main failure risk in this domain.

* Experience with performance measurement or financial calculation libraries, ideally for private markets.
* Experience building versioned, reproducible computation pipelines.

Fifth Dimension is the most prominent AI company in real estate in the world, bringing the magic of AI automation to document-heavy industries . Our AI workspace helps leading investment managers, owners, and operators across the US, UK, and APAC automate complex workflows, extract insights from critical documents, and make faster, smarter decisions.

We're hiring a Forward Deployed Strategist to own delivery on our most important US accounts. You'll work in a pod with a forward deployed engineer, an account manager and our sales team, and you'll make the calls that decide whether a pilot becomes a firm-wide deployment: which workflow comes first, who needs to be in the room, what we build and what we don't. Customers will trust you because you understand their business. Our product team will listen to you because you've seen what works.

**What a week looks like**
--------------------------

**Monday.** Pod reviews across your three US accounts. One is on track. One has an MD asking for a bespoke dashboard. One has gone quiet: asset management hasn't logged in for ten days. You move that one to the top of the week.

**Tuesday.** On site with the quiet account. You sit with two asset managers through quarter-end and find the step that eats a week a month: reconciling operator reports against the rent roll. By the afternoon you've built a first version in the product, on their own documents, and they've told you what it gets wrong.

**Wednesday.** You move the FDE's week onto that workflow and off the dashboard. Then you write to the MD: why the dashboard can wait, what the team gets instead, and when.

**Thursday.** Two hours with our CTO and the FDEs. Three accounts have asked for some version of the same reconciliation. You bring the brief: what's common, what's one customer's preference, and what the template should be.

**Friday.** Three asset managers ran this week's reconciliation in 5D, and nobody opened the spreadsheet. You post the weekly update for each pod: what moved, what's stuck, what you decided. Then you sit in on a sales call with a prospect who has the same problem, to hear how they describe it.

This is a forward-deployed week at Fifth Dimension. You decide what we build for our most important customers, and you make sure they use it. What works in one account becomes product for all of them.

**About Us**
------------

Fifth Dimension builds AI software for the firms that invest in and manage real assets. We help people work with complex documents and business data, from leases and financial models to investment memos. We're a Series A company with offices in London, New York and Singapore.

* Owning delivery at a strategic level on a few of our US enterprise accounts after they sign: the use cases, the plan, the narrative and the decisions.
* Customer-facing for most of the week, often on site with investment, asset management and finance teams.
* Directing forward-deployed engineering time: deciding what our FDEs build and why, and changing course when a rollout stalls.
* The bridge to product: turning what works in one account into templates, skills and workflows that work in every account.
* AI-first. You build with AI yourself, and you can tell a customer exactly where it will and won't help.

**What This Role Is Not**
-------------------------

* A product manager role with a roadmap. You shape the product from the field; you don't own the backlog.
* An engineering role. You don't need to write production code; our FDEs do. You do need to build in the product and understand what's being built.
* Account management or customer success. Your pod has an account manager. You own the strategy, not the calendar.
* Sales. There's no quota. You'll sit in on sales calls to learn the market, not to close.

**The Challenge**
-----------------

A signed pilot is a bet, not a deployment. Real estate investment firms carry decades of process, documents in every format, and teams with good reason to be sceptical of AI. The first use case decides whether the rest of the firm follows.

Get it right and, six weeks in, the team uses it every day, the expansion conversation has started, and the workflow is a template every new customer starts from. Get it wrong and the pilot quietly expires.

new_jobs.description:
Fifth Dimension is the most prominent AI company in real estate in the world, bringing the magic of AI automation to document-heavy industries . Our AI workspace helps leading investment managers, owners, and operators across the US, UK, and APAC automate complex workflows, extract insights from critical documents, and make faster, smarter decisions.

We're hiring a Forward Deployed Strategist to own delivery on our most important US accounts. You'll work in a pod with a forward deployed engineer, an account manager and our sales team, and you'll make the calls that decide whether a pilot becomes a firm-wide deployment: which workflow comes first, who needs to be in the room, what we build and what we don't. Customers will trust you because you understand their business. Our product team will listen to you because you've seen what works.

**What a week looks like**
--------------------------

**Monday.** Pod reviews across your three US accounts. One is on track. One has an MD asking for a bespoke dashboard. One has gone quiet: asset management hasn't logged in for ten days. You move that one to the top of the week.

**Tuesday.** On site with the quiet account. You sit with two asset managers through quarter-end and find the step that eats a week a month: reconciling operator reports against the rent roll. By the afternoon you've built a first version in the product, on their own documents, and they've told you what it gets wrong.

**Wednesday.** You move the FDE's week onto that workflow and off the dashboard. Then you write to the MD: why the dashboard can wait, what the team gets instead, and when.

**Thursday.** Two hours with our CTO and the FDEs. Three accounts have asked for some version of the same reconciliation. You bring the brief: what's common, what's one customer's preference, and what the template should be.

**Friday.** Three asset managers ran this week's reconciliation in 5D, and nobody opened the spreadsheet. You post the weekly update for each pod: what moved, what's stuck, what you decided. Then you sit in on a sales call with a prospect who has the same problem, to hear how they describe it.

This is a forward-deployed week at Fifth Dimension. You decide what we build for our most important customers, and you make sure they use it. What works in one account becomes product for all of them.

**About Us**
------------

Fifth Dimension builds AI software for the firms that invest in and manage real assets. We help people work with complex documents and business data, from leases and financial models to investment memos. We're a Series A company with offices in London, New York and Singapore.

Our values are Own It, Ship It and Don't Be Boring. We move quickly, challenge each other kindly and care about making something customers actually use.

**What This Role Is**
---------------------

* Owning delivery at a strategic level on a few of our US enterprise accounts after they sign: the use cases, the plan, the narrative and the decisions.
* Customer-facing for most of the week, often on site with investment, asset management and finance teams.
* Directing forward-deployed engineering time: deciding what our FDEs build and why, and changing course when a rollout stalls.
* The bridge to product: turning what works in one account into templates, skills and workflows that work in every account.
* AI-first. You build with AI yourself, and you can tell a customer exactly where it will and won't help.

**What This Role Is Not**
-------------------------

* A product manager role with a roadmap. You shape the product from the field; you don't own the backlog.
* An engineering role. You don't need to write production code; our FDEs do. You do need to build in the product and understand what's being built.
* Account management or customer success. Your pod has an account manager. You own the strategy, not the calendar.
* Sales. There's no quota. You'll sit in on sales calls to learn the market, not to close.

**The Challenge**
-----------------

A signed pilot is a bet, not a deployment. Real estate investment firms carry decades of process, documents in every format, and teams with good reason to be sceptical of AI. The first use case decides whether the rest of the firm follows.

Get it right and, six weeks in, the team uses it every day, the expansion conversation has started, and the workflow is a template every new customer starts from. Get it wrong and the pilot quietly expires.
